% Canonical equation macros: reused verbatim by views; science authority is core.
\newcommand{\EqComposition}{\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
\rho_k&=\yin-\Pi_k(\ma),&z_k&=F_k(\rho_k)+B_k(\ma).
\end{aligned}\label{eq:composition}\end{equation}}
\newcommand{\EqMap}{\begin{equation}z_k=A_k\yin-A_k[\Pi_k(\ma)]+B_k(\ma).\label{eq:map}\end{equation}}
\newcommand{\EqLinear}{\begin{equation}D_k:=B_k-A_k\circ\Pi_k,\qquad z_k=A_k\yin+D_k\ma.\label{eq:linear}\end{equation}}
\newcommand{\EqDerivative}{\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
J_{z\leftarrow y,k}^{\mathrm{fixed}}&=\mathrm{D}F_k|_{\rho_k},\\
J_{z\leftarrow m,k}^{\mathrm{fixed}}&=\mathrm{D}B_k|_{\ma}
 -(\mathrm{D}F_k|_{\rho_k})\circ(\mathrm{D}\Pi_k|_{\ma}).
\end{aligned}\label{eq:derivative}\end{equation}}
\newcommand{\EqShift}{\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
\Delta z_k^{\mathrm{model}}&=z_k(m_{\mathrm{ref}}^{\ap}+\delta m_k^{\ap})-z_k(m_{\mathrm{ref}}^{\ap})=D_k\delta m_k^{\ap},\\
b_{z,k}^{\mathrm{model}}&=\mathbb E_{\mathcal L}[D_k\delta m_k^{\ap}\mid\Op]
\quad\text{only with exact bias authority.}
\end{aligned}\label{eq:shift}\end{equation}}

\newcommand{\EqCovariance}{\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
C_z^{\mathrm{FRUIT}}={}&A_kC_{yy}^{\mathrm{FRUIT}}A_k^{\mathsf T}
 +D_kC_{mm}^{\mathrm{FRUIT}}D_k^{\mathsf T}\\
 &+A_kC_{ym}^{\mathrm{FRUIT}}D_k^{\mathsf T}
 +D_kC_{my}^{\mathrm{FRUIT}}A_k^{\mathsf T}.
\end{aligned}\label{eq:covariance}\end{equation}}
\newcommand{\EqNOI}{\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
z_{k,b}^{\mathrm{full}}&=A_k y_{k,b}^{\mathrm{full}}+D_k\ma,\\
\mathbb E_{\mathcal L}[z_{k,b}^{\mathrm{full}}\mid\Op]
 &=A_k\mathbb E_{\mathcal L}[y_{k,b}^{\mathrm{full}}\mid\Op]+D_k\ma,\\
\mathbb E_{\Lnoi}[\delta y_{k,b}^{\mathrm{NOI}}\mid\Onoi]&=0,
&\delta z_{k,b}^{\mathrm{NOI}}&=A_k\delta y_{k,b}^{\mathrm{NOI}}.
\end{aligned}\label{eq:noi}\end{equation}}

\newcommand{\NormEquations}{\Unit{Composition, fixed-state derivatives and model-error transfer}{core:equations}{%
Bind $\Pi_k:M_k\to Y_k$, $F_k:Y_k\to Z_k$, $B_k:M_k\to Z_k$ with
compatible operand pairs, support, reference/gauge/null-space state and all
consequential state. The ordinary conditional composition is
\EqComposition
$\Pi_k(\ma)$ is the removal contribution; $F_k(\rho_k)$ is processed residual;
$B_k(\ma)$ is rejoin contribution. The exact operation graph specifies order,
bypassed operations, removal/rejoin locations and all path application counts.
No inverse, $\Pi_k=B_k$, equal spaces/supports, universal upstream bypass,
model truth or unit response is assumed. Unknown contributions are not zero.

Only when the \emph{complete} $F_k=A_k$ is exact fixed linear on the declared
domain, support and state does distributivity give
\EqMap
Nonlinear $\Pi_k/B_k$ keep this map-valued form. Only when $A_k,\Pi_k,B_k$
are all exact fixed linear maps on compatible vector spaces/coordinates may one use
\EqLinear
A fixed basis or input-dependent internal-coordinate evaluation alone proves
neither complete linearity nor nonlinearity; all centering, support and material state count. Affine offsets
cannot be discarded. Otherwise retain the full composition.

For differentiable fixed numerical maps, the chain rule on exact compatible
tangent/reference/gauge spaces gives
\EqDerivative
Bind baseline, perturbation units/basis, support, tangent domains/codomain,
derivative convention and fixed conditioning. Complete fixed linearity reduces
these maps to $A_k$ and $D_k$. Failed differentiability or branch/support/gauge
comparison makes the derivative unavailable, or permits a separately typed
finite-difference/state-transition object with its own convention. This fixed
derivative never substitutes for RF-03--RF-07.

Under complete fixed linearity, the same input/operators and compatible applied
reference/error space, subtraction of two results gives
\EqShift
Here $D_k$ is the \textbf{model-path transfer operator};
$\Delta z_k^{\mathrm{model}}$ is the \textbf{model-induced output shift}.
These are distinct products, not interchangeable names. Model mismatch is the
declared model/reference discrepancy, not covariance or bias by implication.
Calling the law-qualified expected shift model-induced bias additionally
requires an exact target estimand, reference/truth model, model-error random
variable, probability law and its exact law-relative conditioning. Without those, bias is
unavailable while the declared shift/sensitivity may remain available. Transform
accepted error through its exact acceptance-to-application relation first.
}}
\newcommand{\NormResponseLocal}{\Unit{Response conditioning: fixed maps and state-changing procedures}{core:response-local}{%
Every response record binds role, perturbation source/domain, units, basis,
baseline, codomain, derivative or finite-difference convention, fixed/rerun
state, recurrence/selector extent, operation counts, generations and conditioning.
Baseline/perturbed support, branch and reference/gauge/null-space comparison
shall be explicit. Changed reference is not silently signal. Core declarations
supply no numerical availability.
\begin{description}
\item[RF-01: fixed one-step measured-input response.]
Perturb only $\yin\in Y_k$ while freezing the complete realized
operator-defining state and induced numerical $\Pi_k,F_k,B_k$ maps, applied
model and every other consequential fixed fact. Evaluate every internal
coordinate required by those fixed maps on the perturbed operand; such
coordinates may change. Codomain is the compatible $Z_k$ difference/tangent
space. No defining-state relearning or re-resolution, model learning,
recurrence, stopping or selector rerun belongs to this query. Measured-input
names the iteration-input path, not a new independent measurement.
\item[RF-02: fixed one-step applied-model response.]
Perturb only $\ma\in M_k^{\ap}$ while freezing the complete realized
operator-defining maps/state and measured iteration input. Evaluate every
internal fixed-map coordinate required by the applied-model action, including
its removal, residual-processing and rejoin paths. Codomain is the compatible
$Z_k$ difference/tangent space. Candidate/accepted perturbations must separately
include their transformations. No construction/acceptance, defining-state
learning or re-resolution, recurrence or selector rerun belongs here.
\item[RF-03: one-iteration full-procedure response.]
Perturb the declared one-iteration input with prior $S_k$ and upstream producer
procedure/state fixed. Rerun every method-prescribed operation that can change
the operator-defining map or consequential state: model construction/acceptance,
loading subspace, metric, support/mask, centering/reference, rank, grouping,
selection, threshold, branch or other state-resolution rule. Evaluate required
internal coordinates within the resulting maps. Bind the result codomain and
all state/support/branch transitions; earlier recurrence and terminal selection
are outside this local role.
\end{description}
RF-01/02 evaluate fixed maps; RF-03 reruns prescribed defining-state resolution.
Equal resulting maps do not erase the different causal query. An internal
coordinate change under one fixed map is not RF-03 merely because it is called
an application coefficient. A recomputed quantity that changes defining state/map belongs
to RF-03 or another separately typed procedure query. The declared fixed map
must be established from exact source/state bindings; the admitted PTC
specialization supplies that relation on its stated domain. Insufficient
source/state evidence gives typed unavailability, not a blanket recomputation rule.

Leaving the exact finite/rank/support domain makes the affected fixed response
unavailable or a separately typed transition/discontinuity; it does not
silently become RF-03. Fixed derivatives use the general chain rule and reduce
to $A_k,D_k$ only under complete linearity. A fixed affine operation retains
its offset even when its derivative is linear. Changed method-defining rules
need a new method identity; merely evaluating a fixed map does not.
}}
\newcommand{\NormResponseOuter}{\Unit{Recursive, terminal, whole-chain and parent-domain responses}{core:response-outer}{%
\begin{description}
\item[RF-04: fixed-sequence recursive response.]
Perturb the declared recursion input; fix method rules, initial state, upstream
producer procedure/state and the predeclared sequence or absolute endpoint
index. Propagate input/model/state dependence through that exact fixed extent.
Bind recursion-input and result/sequence codomains and query convention.
Data-dependent sequence length and terminal selection are outside this role.
\item[RF-05: selected-terminal response.]
Perturb the declared procedure/selection input, naming fixed initial/upstream
facts. Include consequential iterations, convergence, stopping, resource
limits and terminal selection. Bind complete candidate population, conversions,
comparison rule, causes, terminal-record identity, selected-result codomain
and query convention. Include branch/support/state/selection transitions.
\item[RF-06: whole-chain response.]
Perturb the exact upstream/source query, naming fixed external facts. Rerun
every included data-dependent upstream producer and the declared FRUIT
procedure, including its recurrence/terminal extent. Bind upstream/final
domains, producer identities and query convention; unavailable included
producer or comparison dependencies remain unavailable.
\item[RF-07: complete FRUIT-only parent-domain response.]
Perturb the realized parent-domain payload while holding upstream producer
operation, learned state and generation fixed. Compose declared parent-domain
entry with the complete FRUIT procedure, including recurrence and terminal
selection as applicable. Bind initial FRUIT conditions, parent/final domains,
query convention and RF-03/RF-04/RF-05 component references. No upstream
producer is rerun. The numerical query payload is not held fixed.
\end{description}
RF-03 is the local one-iteration relation with prior state fixed. RF-04 composes
fixed extent; RF-05 includes stopping/selection extent. RF-07 is the outer
parent-domain composition and references those components, not an independent
alias of any one of them. A one-iteration specialization that reduces to a
component reuses its exact response/status with that specialization recorded.
RF-06 reruns the included upstream producers; RF-07 does not. Equal numerical
values do not erase distinct query identities.

Perturbed parent payloads are separately identified response-query objects
with immutable baseline-parent ancestry. Fixed producer generation neither
mutates the measured parent nor claims a new upstream realization. All roles
retain exact reference/gauge/null-space and branch/support/state/selection
comparison. Threshold or selection boundaries may destroy a derivative;
undefined comparisons, missing results and nonexistent derivatives retain
typed unavailability/discontinuity, with affected scope and cause. A finite
difference needs its own declared step, normalization and comparison contract;
a fixed-branch derivative is not its replacement. No online adaptive filter
or other numerical estimator is introduced.

\textbf{Scoped supersession.} The former RF-07 held-numerical-parent meaning
remains retired. r0.3 replaces r0.2's blanket treatment of internal coordinates as frozen
defining state, and its generic recomputation-to-RF-03 assignment, with the
three exact roles and causal boundaries above. All seven stable RF identities remain.
}}
\newcommand{\NormCovariance}{\Unit{Law-relative stochastic targets and complete joint covariance}{core:covariance}{%
Every target binds \texttt{target\_law\_identity}, random variables, conditioned
fixed objects, resolution/selection condition, omitted variation, support/domain
and reference/gauge/null-space state. $\Op$ means fixed \emph{before the random
event of that exact law} $\mathcal L$, not before every physical or computational
outcome. Bind quantity/units, parent/population/generation, maps/rules, state,
grouping and assumptions explicitly; a generation label is no substitute for
conditioning. Three distinct targets are required:
\begin{description}
\item[Physical/random-parent target.]
The measured parent and every model whose variation is estimated remain random.
Do not condition them on realized numerical values. Preserve all model-learning
variation and parent/model dependence included by this exact law.
\item[Fixed-realized-model target.]
The exact applied model is deliberately conditioned fixed under a separately
named law/target. Its model covariance and parent/model cross blocks vanish
only there; model-learning variation is omitted. This is not equivalent to the
random-model target. The stochastic parent is not silently fixed too.
\item[Conditional NOI-randomization target.]
The realized parent payload, fixed applied model/operator graph, support and
other exact state may be conditioning facts because they precede the declared
NOI assignment/member draw. When its source law conditions on successful design
resolution, retain that exact resolution condition explicitly. This is neither
a physical-parent target nor permission to select favorable FRUIT outcomes.
\end{description}
A branch-, completion-, convergence- or terminal-selection-conditioned FRUIT
target requires a separate method and estimand; it remains unavailable without
separate authority. Do not hide such censoring or a draw-dependent domain in
$\Op$. Record any permitted selection/domain conditioning in its exact source
law and target; no universal physical-parent interpretation is imposed on NOI.

Under complete fixed linearity, compatible real vector coordinates, finite
joint second moments and exact law/conditioning, define $C_{yy}^{\mathrm{FRUIT}},
C_{mm}^{\mathrm{FRUIT}},C_{ym}^{\mathrm{FRUIT}},C_{my}^{\mathrm{FRUIT}}$ as the
conditional covariance blocks of $(\yin,\ma)$ under
$\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathcal L}[\cdot\mid\Op]$. Axes bind quantity, units,
support and reference/gauge/null-space coordinates; $m$ is applied model.
\EqCovariance
For a real joint covariance $C_{my}^{\mathrm{FRUIT}}=(C_{ym}^{\mathrm{FRUIT}})^{\mathsf T}$.
Both cross terms remain unless the exact law/conditioning justifies omission.
A parent-learned model is not independent by implication. Fixed gauge or a
singular covariance does not mean an unavailable absolute mode was measured
with zero uncertainty. Nonlinear/random-operator propagation or a Jacobian
approximation requires its own typed method; it is not this exact identity.
Accepted uncertainty reaches applied space only through the exact transformation
and dependence. Repeated shared-parent iterations are not independent observations
and imply no inverse-square-root iteration-count uncertainty law.
}}

\newcommand{\NormNOI}{\Unit{NOI target-law members, full-product action and source binding}{core:noi}{%
For complete fixed linearity and explicitly fixed applied model/operators/state,
full parent realizations and zero-target-law NOI members have distinct actions:
\EqNOI
Here $k$ is absolute iteration, $b$ the member, and $g$ the ensemble generation.
Bind each object's full versus NOI role, exact parent/output domain, units,
support/reference/gauge/null-space, target law and center convention.
$\mathcal L$ in the full-product expectation is its separately declared law;
$\Lnoi$ is the exact conditional NOI design/assignment law and $\Onoi$ its
fixed-parent/model/operator/support/design-resolution conditioning. These are
role-qualified symbols, not PTC transformed signal or the result-space $Z_k$.

The zero is a \textbf{target-law expectation}. No member is required to have
zero sample or spatial mean. No finite-ensemble mean subtraction, member-wise
centering or $B-1$ correction is implied. Source and deterministic residual
structure may remain in individual members. The deterministic $D_k\ma$ term
shall not be added to each zero-target-law member. It belongs to the full product
and its exact law-qualified center.

The exact content-bound owner source is
\texttt{OWNER\_INTERIM\_CORRECTION\_R0.2.txt}, section 2, with its directive
identity/digest in the source record and preserved r0.2 archive bound on each cover. It authorizes this conditional
zero-target-law distinction; it does not supply a complete external numerical
NOI law or estimator. An actual source-law identity/digest, random event,
conditioning/design resolution, ensemble generation, exact NOI-owned product
and estimator binding remain \texttt{unavailable\_external\_binding} until
supplied through separately approved authority. A symbolic $\Lnoi$ is not an
admitted law instance. Where an exact law supplies known-zero second moments,
use its quantity-appropriate zero-target-law action and estimator convention.
No numerical FRUIT/NOI route follows from the equation.

Every boundary names member meaning: full parent realization, zero-target-law
NOI member, residual, complete FRUIT output or another exact quantity. A
full-affine-member method requires exact member/transformed centers, source-law
and estimator authority, centering/second-moment convention, response/support
parity and a separately bound method. No finite-ensemble centering is inferred.

Fixed-state NOI requires exact application, response and support parity and
explicit omitted learning/support/selection/stopping/restart/leakage variation.
NOI-informed later learning creates a dependent immutable science/ensemble/
uncertainty successor, not independent validation or retroactive editing.
Per-realization relearning of model/support/cleaner/operator-defining coefficients/stopping/selector
is a distinct method and ensemble with complete member-state graph. New values
under unchanged rules produce new states, not a method each. No mixing/pooling
of fixed and relearned members is authorized here. FLT and other parent routes
retain exact producer quantities and response authority; no filter inverse,
route permission or interchangeability is supplied by FRUIT/NOI naming.
}}


\newcommand{\EqPTC}{\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
G^{\rm app}_{g,t}&=\widehat A_g^{\mathsf T}W^{\rm app}_{g,t}\widehat A_g,
&\widehat m^{\rm app}_{g,t}(x)&=x_{g,t}W^{\rm app}_{g,t}\widehat A_g(G^{\rm app}_{g,t})^+,\\
P^{\rm PTC}_{g,t,\Theta}&=I-W^{\rm app}_{g,t}\widehat A_g(G^{\rm app}_{g,t})^+\widehat A_g^{\mathsf T},\\
z_{g,t}&=x_{g,t}-\widehat m^{\rm app}_{g,t}(x)\widehat A_g^{\mathsf T}
=x_{g,t}P^{\rm PTC}_{g,t,\Theta},
&\delta z_{g,t}&=\delta x_{g,t}P^{\rm PTC}_{g,t,\Theta}.
\end{aligned}\label{eq:ptc-map}\end{equation}}
\newcommand{\EqPTCAffine}{\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
x_{g,t}&=Y^{\rm CAL}_{g,t}-\lambda_g,\\
z_{g,t}&=(Y^{\rm CAL}_{g,t}-\lambda_g)P^{\rm PTC}_{g,t,\Theta},
&\mathrm D_Yz[H]&=HP^{\rm PTC}_{g,t,\Theta}.
\end{aligned}\label{eq:ptc-affine}\end{equation}}
\newcommand{\NormOperatorRoles}{\Unit{Operator-defining state and internal application coordinates}{core:operator-roles}{%
Every use of ``coefficient'' shall identify its scientific role. Three classes
are distinct; numerical changes alone do not classify the response.
\begin{description}
\item[A. Operator-defining state and coefficients.]
These determine the complete induced input-output map and are fixed in RF-01/02.
For the admitted PTC application bind loading subspace $\widehat A_g$,
application metric/influence $W^{\rm app}_{g,t}$, normal matrix $G^{\rm app}_{g,t}$
and its generalized inverse, fixed centering/reference $\lambda_g$,
detector/group binding, application/output support, rank requirement and frozen
tolerance, mask, projection orientation/family, branch, generation and every
other fact changing the induced map. A fixed structure alone does not fix
unresolved defining state.
\item[B. Input-dependent internal application coordinates.]
These intermediate solves are functions evaluated from the perturbed operand
while A-class facts remain fixed. PTC's $\widehat m^{\rm app}_{g,t}(x)$ is
such a modal coordinate. Its changed value alone is not operator-defining coefficient relearning,
operator re-resolution, a changed method/operator generation or RF-03.
It is evaluation of the same map. Preserve its operand/query/value bindings;
it is not the FRUIT applied feedback model.
\item[C. Frozen numerical removed component.]
A component $\widehat U$ computed from one parent and then held numerically
fixed under perturbation defines the separately named affine subtraction
family $\mathcal A^{\rm sub}_{\widehat U}(Y')=Y'-\widehat U$ with
$\mathrm D\mathcal A^{\rm sub}_{\widehat U}[H]=H$. It is not ordinary
fixed-subspace projection and is not the base PTC PCA/SVD application rule.
\end{description}
Relearning or resolving an A-class fact is procedure variation. Evaluating a
B-class coordinate is fixed-map application. Holding a C-class component fixed
is a different named affine operation. The seven operation-state categories
remain; these three roles clarify their contents, not three new lifecycle states.
No family, rank, support, method or route is selected, and no response fidelity
is established by this conditional classification.
}}
\newcommand{\NormPTCMap}{\Unit{Exact admitted PTC fixed-subspace specialization}{core:ptc-map}{%
For one exact frozen group/time application state, substitute the admitted
PTC modal-coordinate equation into its output equation. All symbols in this
section are PTC-local; $z_{g,t}$ is the upstream operation's output, not by
itself the complete FRUIT result $z_k$.
\EqPTC
The identity $I$ acts on the exact detector row domain. Bind all matrix axes
and the source's detector-right orientation. $\Theta$ denotes all A-class
facts, including $G$ and its generalized inverse. The coordinate
$\widehat m^{\rm app}(x)$ is reevaluated algebraically when $x$ changes;
$P^{\rm PTC}_{g,t,\Theta}$ remains fixed. This establishes the fixed-state
input response for that operation, within RF-01 for its declared fixed-map use.
A full FRUIT response must compose its actual typed path maps; this local
identity does not replace that composition or authorize a parent route.

For the uncentered calibrated input and fixed additive reference:
\EqPTCAffine
This map is fixed affine, not strictly linear in $Y^{\rm CAL}$ by implication.
The term $-\lambda_gP^{\rm PTC}_{g,t,\Theta}$ remains part of the output.
Its derivative is detector-right multiplication by $P$, unlike the identity
input derivative of frozen-component subtraction. No numerical equality of
one output makes those operations interchangeable.

The source admits the solve only when every required input and $G^{\rm app}$
are finite and $\operatorname{rank}_{\tau_g}(G^{\rm app})=k_{{\rm req},g}$
under exact frozen tolerance, with exact application/output support. The
same admitted domain applies to the perturbation. Leaving it yields affected
unavailability/cause or a separately typed transition; it does not silently
change the RF role, reduce rank, fill data or borrow detectors.

If perturbation reruns centering, subspace, metric, support/mask, detector
binding, rank/tolerance, grouping, selection or another defining-state rule,
the query is RF-03 or another separately typed procedure response. If exact
source/state is insufficient to establish $P$ for a particular case, that
case remains unavailable. PTC owns the estimator and its map; FRUIT owns only
the response-role assignment to a declared use. No estimator, PTC family,
rank/support rule, numerical FRUIT method/route or response fidelity is changed
or approved by this source-derived crosswalk.
}}
